chunks: From him, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Khālid, from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said: When should I perform the ʿAṣr salat (prayer) when I am not traveling? He said: “At the measure of two-thirds of a foot after al-Ẓuhr.”

key_terms.أُصَلِّيهَا: I perform it; I pray it
key_terms.الْعَصْرُ: the ʿAṣr salat (prayer), the afternoon obligatory prayer
key_terms.بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ: after al-Ẓuhr, after the noon prayer time
key_terms.ثُلُثَيْ قَدَمٍ: two-thirds of a foot, a classical measure used to indicate prayer time

ai.seo_question: When should ʿAṣr salat (prayer) be performed when one is not traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the time for performing the ʿAṣr salat (prayer) for a resident who is not traveling. It indicates that ʿAṣr is to be performed after al-Ẓuhr with a delay measured as two-thirds of a foot, expressing the prescribed prayer timing in classical legal terminology.
